title: Explainable AI
lines: Explainable AI treats explanations as claims that need evidence, rather than persuasive model narratives.
The book begins by asking what is being explained and who needs the answer.
A debugging engineer, affected person, and system owner may require different kinds of understanding.
Its distinctive treatment follows those differences through methods, validation, foundation models, and complete agent systems.
You will learn why an attractive heat map or rationale cannot certify itself.
The final chapters develop explanation contracts that another process can inspect and attempt to falsify.

title: Choose the question first
lines: An explanation begins with a target, an audience, and a claim to be tested.
A developer may need to locate a defect in a model.
An affected person may need to understand a decision and possible routes of challenge.
An operator may need evidence about behavior across a deployment setting.
The book calls for an explicit explanation contract before selecting a technique.
That opening changes the reading task from collecting visualizations to matching evidence with a purpose.

title: Attribution has a scope
lines: Attribution methods investigate how selected inputs relate to a particular model output.
Their results depend on choices about comparisons, approximations, and the method's assumptions.
A colorful map can be useful while answering a narrower question than viewers expect.
The book compares these techniques without turning one graphic into universal understanding.
Readers learn to ask what was measured and which alternatives were considered.
This prepares the central test of whether the explanation actually tracks the model.

title: A possible change is not enough
chapter: A possible change is not enough
lines: Counterfactual explanations consider changes associated with a different outcome under specified conditions.
The nearest mathematical change may still be unavailable to a real person.
Feasible recourse requires attention to constraints, actions, and the setting around the model.
The book also examines concepts and training data as different explanatory objects.
These approaches answer related questions without becoming interchangeable measures of the same thing.
The chapter sequence helps readers see why method choice follows the explanation contract.

title: Explanations face experiments
lines: The validation chapters ask explanations to survive tests beyond visual plausibility.
If model parameters are randomized, an explanation should respond when its claimed basis disappears.
Other tests examine sensitivity, fidelity, human use, or behavior under changing conditions.
No single test can certify every property an audience might care about.
The book therefore assembles evidence around a specific claim and intended use.
Its practical lesson is to evaluate explanations as carefully as the predictions they accompany.

title: Rationale is another output
lines: Foundation models intensify the temptation to confuse a fluent account with direct introspection.
A generated rationale is itself an output requiring evidence about what it represents.
The book contrasts this with investigations involving activations, interventions, and causal hypotheses.
Even an informative intervention supports conclusions only within its assumptions and experimental scope.
A growing map of internal behavior is not complete understanding of the whole system.
This distinction makes the later chapters more useful than a promise that models can simply explain themselves.

title: Explain the whole system
lines: An agent's result can depend on retrieval, tools, memory, permissions, and surrounding software.
Explaining only the model may leave those consequential dependencies out of view.
The book follows explanation into trajectories, replay, multimodal evidence, and system level assurance.
Formal guarantees also apply within specified boundaries rather than proving universal reliability.
Readers learn to connect an observed result with the processes that produced it.
That wider view returns the discussion to the original contract between an explanation and its audience.

title: Contracts that can expire
lines: The final movement develops explanations as inspectable hypotheses with explicit supporting evidence.
A model update or changed environment can weaken an earlier explanation's validity.
The proposed architecture separates prediction, observation, explanation, validation, and presentation responsibilities.
It asks what another process could inspect, query, or attempt to falsify.
This is a research direction with design choices to examine, not automatic certification.
The reader gains a way to connect established methods with more checkable explanatory systems.

title: Read for your audience
lines: Start by writing down who needs an explanation and what decision it should support.
Read the explanation contract before moving to attribution, counterfactuals, or internal mechanisms.
Use the validation chapters to challenge the evidence behind your preferred method.
The later agent and contract chapters broaden that discipline to complete systems.
Explainable AI is worth reading for this connection between purpose, method, and warranted confidence.
It helps you ask what an explanation establishes before deciding how persuasive it looks.
